newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos says keeping polls choice open.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos says keeping polls choice open.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday he was keeping his options open on who to endorse as his successor and urged aspirants to stop jockeying for support as elections remained over a year away.
"All of this speculation about who is the 'anointed' ... these are all premature and as far as I am concerned unproductive, even counter-productive," Ramos told his weekly news conference.
He was referring to widely reported maneouverings by a number of aspirants to gain his endorsement for the May 1998 presidential election.
The 68-year-old Ramos is barred from contesting for a second term by constitutional provision which limits the president to one six-year term without re-election.
Ramos said that instead of politicking, would-be presidential contenders should look beyond 1998 and work to make the economy competitive in the coming millenium.
"I would like to remind all 'wannabes' to look at it in that light," he said, using local media slang to refer to politicians who want to become president.
"That (presidential election) is still too far, " he added.
Asked if he would endorse a candidate, Ramos said: "That's an option and I am keeping my options open."
Manila newspapers have named at least six politicians who are expected to make a serious bid for the presidency.

They include Vice-President Joseph Estrada, Defence Secretary Renato de Villa, House of Representatives Speaker Jose de Venecia, opposition senators Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, Edgardo Angara and Miriam Santiago, a former judge whom Ramos narrowly defeated in a seven-way presidential contest in 1992.

Officers of two citizens groups calling for an amendment to the constitution to enable Ramos to run for a second term said on Wednesday they would push ahead with their campaign despite the president's recent illness.
Ramos underwent a major operation two weeks ago for the removal of what doctors said was a life-threatening cholesterol blockage in an artery supplying blood to his brain.
"We believe President is God-mandated to lead this country," said Jose Calida, president of the group called Lagda (Signature).
Lagda is one of two groups which have announced plans to collect at least five million signatures starting January 25 to force a plebiscite that would amend the charter.
